name: Major Transit Service Area
description:
A polygon feature layer representing ½ mile (2640 feet) distance walksheds from Major Transit Stops. Derived as a View from SDCI Transit Stop Walksheds layer.
 
 
As per Ordinance 127376, “Transit service area, major” means an area within 2,640 feet walking distance of a stop served by a major transit service, as shown on a map adopted by Director's Rule (DR 01-2026). 

“Transit stop, major” means a stop on a major transit service. 
 
“Transit service, major” means the following transit services:  
1. Commuter rail; 
2. Light rail or street car systems; and 
3. Bus rapid transit routes that are in operation or are funded for development and projected for construction within an applicable six-year transit plan under RCW 35.58.2795
 
Resources
Ordinance 127376
Seattle Municipal Code section 23.54.015 Table B
Seattle Municipal Code section 23.44.017
Seattle Municipal Code section 23.84A.038 "T"

name: Seattle Bus Volumes
description:
A line feature layer derived from the Metro Transportation Network (TNET) King County. Each line segment represents a unique link in the King County transportation network. More information about TNET, including field metadata can be found in the King County GIS Catalogue.

This layer is a simplified version of the TNET that is filtered for segments in Seattle where public bus transit service operates. Five fields are joined to the TNET layer representing the number of daily in-service buses that are scheduled to travel on the segment each weekday. 

Joined fields:

  • CHANGE_NUM - Unique integer that identifies service change period. 157 = Fall 2024
  • TRIP_KIND_CD - S = service trip
  • SCHED_DAY_TYPE_CODED_NUM - 0 = weekday
  • DAILY_TRIP_CNT - The number of times per day the given t-link is traversed by buses meeting all criteria in the given row.
  • ROUTES – Bus routes included in the DAILY_TRIP_CNT

This data can be used to view scheduled in-service weekday bus volumes in Seattle by street segment and is reported in SDOT’s Annual Traffic Report. The current published layer represents bus volume data from the Fall 2024 service change (September 2024 – March 2025) and may be out of date with current service levels. Data will be refreshed annually with the update of the Annual Traffic Report. If you need more recent data, please contact King County.

Maintained by Seattle Department of Transportation

Refresh Cycle: Static, manually updated as required

Contact: SDOT Transit and Mobility team

name: King County Tax Parcel Polygons with select City of Seattle geographic overlays
description:
King County Assessor Tax Parcel polygons with selected King County Assessor (KCA) data and City of Seattle spatial overlay data to support land use planning functions. Displayed as all intersecting polygons from input layers, including the rights-of-way.

King County Assessor data has been summarized to the tax parcel identification number (PIN) and City of Seattle spatial overlay data has been assigned through geographic overlay processes.  This data is updated quarterly and is used to support the analytical and reporting functions of the City of Seattle long-range and policy planning office.

The spatial overlays include:
City of Seattle Land Use Zoning
Shoreline (to identify water/land portions of parcels)
Comprehensive Plan Regional and Urban Centers
City Parks Boundaries
Census Blocks 2010/2020
City Landmarks
Public Ownership (as identified through taxpayer name)
General (10)/Planning (20) Categories of Existing Land Use (may not match uses described in the City of Seattle Municipal Code)

This layer represents the intersections of all the polygons listed above, therefore the tax parcel polygon may be represented by separate polygons if split by another spatial layer. Please use caution when using the tax assessor attribute data from this layer.

Special note regarding King County Assessor data:
KCA tax parcels are created by King County for property tax assessment and collection and may not match development sites as defined by the City of Seattle (single buildings may span multiple tax parcels), may be stacked on top of each other to represent undivided interest and vertical parcels, or may be made up of several sites that are not contiguous.  Every effort is made to accurately summarize key tax parcel attributes to a single PIN.  

Please be aware that the King County Assessor site address is not a postal address and may not match other address sources for the same property such as postal, utility billing, and permitting.

This grouped layer uses data from DWW.WQS_PV(point features) and DWW.polygon_plgn_pv(polygon features).   To display the polygons the  following query is used, PLY_LIFECYCLE_CODE in ( 'C', 'PC', 'UNK', 'T', 'TBC', 'U') and PLY_DWW_FEATYPE_CODE = 'WQS'.  Labels are based on the attribute DESCRIPTION.  The point features uses this query, WQS_PV_LIFECYCLE_CODE in ('C', 'PC', 'UNK', 'T', 'TBC', 'U').  Labels are based on the attributes WQS_PV_FEA_TYPE and WQS_PV_FEATYPE_DESC.  Included are layers for the Proposed assets, and separately the Abandoned/Removed assets. The features and associated labels do not display when zoomed out beyond 1:10,000.   Maintained by SPU GIS DWW Data Maintenance staff.
Refreshed weekly.

name: Lifelong Recreation Programming Sites
description:
Displays Seattle Parks and Recreation's (SPR) Lifelong Recreation's programming locations, including general ages 50+, Rainbow, Dementia Friendly, and Outdoor Recreation programs. Lifelong Recreation programs focus on physical activity, social engagement, education, arts, creativity, and healthy lifestyles, and are offered for older adult (50 and over) populations. Data is maintained and updated by Lifelong Recreation staff internally and intended to be shared for public-facing webpage publication and use.

Refresh Cycle: Weekly
 
Feature Class: DPR.LLR_Programming_PT

name: ECA - Steep Slope
description:
Displays areas with 40% steep slope or greater in the City of Seattle.
 
A polygon feature class showing areas with an incline of 40% or more (10 feet of vertical rise over a horizontal distance of 25 feet or less) with a height of at least 10 feet. 
 
This layer was produced using a combination of 2001 LIDAR contours (Puget Sound LIDAR Consortium) and the 1993 topographic contours from aerial photos. The Steep Slope layer was most recently updated under SDCI Director's Rule 12-2019.
 
The steep slope area map is called “advisory” because the mapping is used by the Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections for initial information and screening. Whether or not a site is eventually treated as an environmentally critical area is based on the actual topography of the ground surface.
 
For more information about the definition of steep slope erosion hazard areas, see Seattle Municipal Code section 25.09.012, Environmentally Critical Areas (ECA) definitions.

name: ECA - Flood Prone Area
description:
FEMA flood prone areas with 100 foot buffer. Original flood prone areas where table digitized into the City of Seattle GIS CGDB control layer in the mid 90's. Layer may be used without the buffer by unselecting the flood = 1 feature type.
 
This layer is used by the City as an aid to evaluate construction sites for the presence of flood prone areas pertinent to Environmentally Critical Areas (ECA)  regulations.
 
Areas that would likely be covered with or carry water as a result of a one hundred (100) year flood event, or that would have a one percent (1%) or greater chance of being covered with or of carrying water in any given year based on current circumstances or maximum development permitted under existing zoning.
 
For more information about the definition of flood prone areas, see Seattle Municipal Code section 25.09.012, Environmentally Critical Areas (ECA) definitions. 
 
Updated as needed.

name: ECA - Liquefaction Prone Area
description:
Displays areas with liquefaction zones.
 
A polygon feature class that shows liquefaction zones. Used to implement and regulate the City of Seattle's Environmentally Critical Areas (ECA) policies. This layer was created in 1995 using data obtained from the USGS. Some edits were made to the edges to better coincide with the City's two foot contour data.
 
Areas of the City subject to ground shaking from seismic hazards that are addressed by Title 22.
 
The Seattle Fault zone as delineated in Troost et al., 2005, The geologic map of Seattle, a progress report, U.S. Geological Survey, Open-file report 2005-1252 , or as the Director determines is more accurately mapped by the U.S. Geological Survey, as set out in a Director's Rule.
 
For more information about the definition of liquefaction zones, see Seattle Municipal Code section 25.09.012, Environmentally Critical Areas (ECA) definitions. 
 
Updated as needed.

name: ECA - Known Slide (Scarp)
description:
This group layer includes point, line, and polygon symbology to display the landslide event inventory. Used to implement and regulate the City of Seattle's Environmentally Critical Areas (ECA) policies. This layer includes a more comprehensive collection of slide events maintained by Shannon and Wilson via the Seattle Landslide Study which included slide data through June 1999.  

The Known Slide layer was most recently updated under SDCI Director's Rule 12-2019.

For more information about the definition of known slide areas, see Seattle Municipal Code section 25.09.012, Environmentally Critical Areas (ECA) definitions.

Updates as needed.
